campaign_name: Brooklyn Bridge — material and arrangement evidence
purpose: Close the open questions that documents could not. This model reached 45 passing tests with 12 placeholders left, and the survivors are not dimensional gaps that a better drawing would fill -- they are questions about what things are MADE OF and how they are ARRANGED, which is exactly what a photograph settles. Every material rule for the deck, the promenade and the stairs is graded D because no registered source says what the surfaces are. OQ-007 records that the approach supports are the wrong KIND of object. OQ-016 asks how the masonry above the saddle is arranged. A person reviewing openly-licensed photographs can answer all three; no amount of re-reading the 1877 report can.

area.note: Midspan of the main span, roughly. A 1.2 km radius reaches both towers, both anchorages and the DUMBO approach. The coordinate is for SEARCH ONLY and is not a control: OQ-008 records that this repository has no sourced position for the bridge axis, and a search centre must never become one.

categories.label: masonry
categories.help: Tower or anchorage stonework close enough to tell granite from limestone, and to see the coursing SRC-002 describes. Feeds MAT-002 and MAT-003.

categories.label: arcade
categories.help: The approach viaduct from below or beside. OQ-007: the model draws slender bents, but SRC-004 describes brick piers and arches. This is the category that settles what actually carries the approach.

categories.label: cornice
categories.help: The tower top above the saddle. OQ-016: the model opens the masonry across the cable corridor because SRC-002 says the cables pass THROUGH the towers, but nothing dimensions the opening.

categories.label: saddle
categories.help: Where a main cable crosses a tower. Shows how much of the cable is visible above the masonry -- the thing that looked wrong in the render.

categories.label: truss
categories.help: A transverse or oblique view of the stiffening trusses. OQ-002: their spacing across the 85 ft deck is a placeholder. A photograph cannot measure it, but it can show how many there are and roughly where they sit.

categories.label: cable
categories.help: Main cable, suspenders, diagonal stays, cable bands. Wrapping, galvanising and the stay arrangement that SRC-002 annotates.

categories.label: deck
categories.help: The roadway surface and its framing. MAT-009 is graded D because no read source says what the wearing surface is.

categories.label: promenade
categories.help: The walkway decking. MAT-010 is D even though every photograph shows timber, because 'wood deck' in SRC-011 is a TYPOLOGY NAME and not a materials statement. A reviewed photograph is what changes that honestly.

categories.label: stair
categories.help: The Washington Street stair down to DUMBO, or the Manhattan approach stair. Their location is sourced; their form is not. OQ-015.

categories.label: railing
categories.help: Promenade railings, fencing and the balustrade. Not yet modelled at all.

categories.label: lighting
categories.help: Lamp standards on the promenade. Not modelled; the brief lists them under details.

categories.label: context
categories.help: A good overall view that shows the bridge in its setting but settles no single component. Useful for the compare panel, weak as evidence.

temporal_note: A 'renewed' subject is replaced on a maintenance cycle, so a photograph of it describes only the day it was taken. A 'stable' subject is substantially original fabric, so an archival frame is still evidence about it. This corpus spans 1867 to 2026; without the distinction a 1905 photograph could silently justify a claim about today's roadway.
